conviction_note: Nothing found that the market has not seen. The bar is Telenor's own compiled consensus (adj. EBITDA 8,603m), put together on 14 October after the company's 22 September housekeeping note had already flagged Q3 as the peak-opex quarter. Grameenphone's Q3 is already out. The peer read-throughs (Elisa's Finland, Telia's Norway mobile intake) lean slightly negative and are proxies, so p_up is 46 on an abs_move of 5.5. findings.finding: Grameenphone's Q3 is already public: NOK adj. EBITDA 1,827m vs 1,960m (-6.8% in NOK, flat organic including a NOK 20m one-off), capex 423m vs 255m. About a fifth of the group's EBITDA is therefore pre-released and roughly in line with the 'only modest improvement' the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Grameenphone release days have moved TEL between -0.71% and +0.75% (26 Oct 2026: -0.71%); the group-day moves are driven by the Nordics and the guide
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: it was published two sessions ago and the stock moved -0.71%. Filed so the segment is not counted again on the day.
findings.independence: Matches the company's own housekeeping guidance of 'only modest improvement in Grameenphone' (https://www.telenor.com/investors/reports-and-information/analyst-coverage-and-consensus/quarterly-housekeeping-items/)

findings.finding: Elisa's Q3 (21 Oct) reports 'slightly intensified competition' in Finnish mobile, post-paid churn up to 18.7% (16.7%), post-paid subscriptions -16,300 and comparable EBITDA -2%. That is a negative read-across to DNA, which Telenor said in September would see easier comps from mid-Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Finland drove the Q1 2026 miss and cut (-5.67%) and part of the Q2 miss (-11.64%), together with Norway
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the consensus file is dated 14 Oct, a week before Elisa reported, so any analyst who did not update after Elisa still carries the improving-comps view. If it were fully priced, TEL would have lagged on 21 Oct; it fell 0.9% that day, which is consistent but not conclusive. DNA is roughly 15-20% of Nordic EBITDA, so this is sized net of the rest of the group.
findings.independence: Telenor's own housekeeping: 'the market remains highly competitive' in Finland, new-sales ARPU recovery modest (https://www.telenor.com/investors/reports-and-information/analyst-coverage-and-consensus/quarterly-housekeeping-items/)

findings.finding: Telia's Q3 (22 Oct) says Norway returned to EBITDA growth on fixed price adjustments and that 'mobile customer intake strengthened'. Telenor Norway's Q2 problem was B2C mobile churn and promotions, so a competitor gaining mobile intake in Q3 is a mild negative for Telenor Norway's subscriber line, partly offset by evidence of rational fixed pricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Norway B2C mobile softness was the lead cause in the Q2 release that fell 11.64%
findings.why_not_priced: The market read Telia as a sector positive (Telia +4.8%, TEL +2.1% on 22 Oct), which suggests it priced the sector tone rather than the share shift inside Norway. If it had priced the share shift, TEL would not have risen with Telia that day. Weak: a proxy, and it lands on one unit.
findings.independence: Telenor housekeeping: 'One competitor has been particularly active with large device discounts for the summer campaigns' in Norway (https://www.telenor.com/investors/reports-and-information/analyst-coverage-and-consensus/quarterly-housekeeping-items/)

findings.finding: Tele2's Q3 (20 Oct) was in line, with organic EBITDAaL guidance narrowed to 4-5% and record cash flow. The Swedish market is healthy, a small positive read for Telenor Sweden, which the company calls a 'fairly stable performer'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sweden has not been the swing line in recent Telenor reactions
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public a week ago, and Sweden was already expected to be stable. A small, separate unit.

findings.finding: On 8 October a nationwide Telenor voice outage of about four hours blocked calls to the emergency services, and Nkom raised preparedness and opened a supervisory inspection (tilsyn) of Telenor. This is a Q4 event, so it may appear as commentary, customer compensation or regulatory risk in the release; it does not touch Q3 numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent in the baseline; TEL fell 0.9% and 1.3% on 8-9 Oct
findings.original_quote: Nasjonal kommunikasjonsmyndighet (Nkom) hever beredskapen og varsler tilsyn mot Telenor
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced in the 8-9 Oct drift. The open question is any compensation or sanction quantification in the release, which is likely small against NOK 33bn of EBITDA.

findings.finding: Telenor ASA was formally charged on 15 Sept (Sanctions Act, aiding and abetting crimes against humanity, former Myanmar operations), and on 17 Sept Asker og Bærum tingrett admitted a class action on behalf of at least 1,253 Myanmar customers. The Q3 report may carry a contingent-liability note or provision.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 15 Sept inside-information release; no results-day precedent
findings.why_not_priced: The charge and the lawsuit are public. What is not known is whether the release quantifies any exposure. A provision would be a one-off below adjusted EBITDA with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.

baseline_tension: No tension: the lean (+0.06) and the run-up (-1.2% over 20 days, -5.6% over 60) are flat, and the small negative peer proxies neither contradict nor beat them. The stock has already de-rated through two guidance cuts.
language_note: e24 (Norwegian) carried the 8 Oct nationwide voice outage and Nkom's tilsyn ('varsler tilsyn mot Telenor'), which none of the English sources searched carried.

e24/NRK (Norwegian) carried the admission of the Myanmar class action by Asker og Bærum tingrett (17 Sept, at least 1,253 claimants); the English sources carried only the company's own charge announcement.
Otherwise nothing beyond the English sources: Telenor publishes every NewsWeb release in English and Norwegian at once, and the decisive document (the IR consensus and housekeeping) is English.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the Grameenphone pre-release finding moved from -0.1 to 0.0.

'The move is in the guide' plus the understatement rule: abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 5.5. Guidance has been cut at two straight prints, the last four results-day moves were 5.7-11.6%, and Q3 numbers are not pre-released. p_up unchanged at 46, so expected_move_pct went from -0.40 to -0.44.
'Coverage tells you which regime': at >13 analysts with a company-compiled consensus, the proxy findings stay small and none was enlarged.
